audit.why: 54.18% over 1460 games with the packet chart giving Olaf the first six rows; EVEN / 6-10 is defensible for a lane that flips on tank scaling.

audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 4-5 and first item said Skill in both layers while the packet chart gives Olaf both, and 2+ items said Olaf while the packet says Skill and the adjacent prose says Sion reclaims it.
audit.why: The chart told the reader momentum was contested exactly where Olaf is strongest, and safe exactly where Sion catches up — the inverse of the data and of the prose beside it.
audit.corrected: phases[3]/[5]/[6].side and win[3]/[5]/[6] flipped in matched pairs, ratings moved to follow, all three phase whys rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page named no Sion ability (packet defect), called Roar of the Slayer a 'shield-break poke', and said Ragnarok 'strips'/'deletes' the charged Q knockup.
audit.why: Roar of the Slayer is an armour-shredding slow shockwave — nothing in it touches shields — and its real quirk is that firing it through a minion KNOCKS THAT MINION BACK through you, extending the poke and shredding your armour from outside your range. Ragnarok's Riot text grants immunity to disables while attacking; Decimating Smash applies a stun AND a knockup, and the knockup half is a displacement the text does not cover.
audit.corrected: Named Glory in Death, Decimating Smash (10s), Soul Furnace and Roar of the Slayer; corrected the E description and added the minion-knockback; narrowed every Ragnarok claim to the stun; added Glory in Death's revive to the late text since 'killing him' is not the end of the fight.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization said to rush Executioner's Calling because 'his healing fights your pattern'.
audit.why: Sion has no lane healing. The only heal in his kit is on Glory in Death, which happens after he dies.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal line rewritten to point at the revive instead of an imaginary lane sustain.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1] ('R to cleanse his charged Q') and dosFull[2] ('E for true damage') both carried bodies about something else.
audit.why: Neither entry supported its own heading.

edits.before: Sion is exactly the immobile melee you farm: no dash to dodge your Q, so your axe-slow sticks every time and your passive ramps attack speed as you take his poke. The one thing to respect is his charged Q — if you stand in it while he winds up, the knockup interrupts your all-in, so trade when it's on cooldown or bait it then step in. At 2-3, Q-slow into E true damage bursts him before his W shield is big enough to eat it.
edits.after: Sion is exactly the immobile melee you farm: no dash to dodge your Q, so your axe-slow sticks every time and your passive ramps attack speed as you take his poke. Respect two things — a charged Decimating Smash stuns and knocks up, so trade on its 10s cooldown or bait it and step in, and Roar of the Slayer fired through a minion knocks that minion into you and shreds your armour. At 2-3, Q-slow into E bursts him before Soul Furnace is big enough to eat it.

edits.before: This is your takeover window. Keep chaining Q pickups to perma-slow him so he can't walk to last-hits, and E him whenever it's up — that true damage cuts straight through the armor he's stacking. At 6, Ragnarok is the whole matchup: it deletes his charged Q knockup, the only tool he has to stop your dive, so once your ult is up you all-in or tower-dive on his CC cooldown and he simply can't peel.
edits.after: This is your takeover window. Keep chaining Q pickups to perma-slow him so he can't walk to last-hits, and E him whenever it's up — that true damage cuts straight through the armor he's stacking. At 6, Ragnarok is the whole matchup: while you keep swinging you are immune to the stun on his charged Decimating Smash, the only tool he has to stop your dive, so all-in on its cooldown and he cannot peel.

edits.before: Sion is the rare tank who reclaims this lane late, not early — once he has two items his W shield, raw HP, and zombie passive turn him into a sponge your flat E true damage can't burn through fast enough, and he stops caring about your short fights. Don't let it get there: convert your early-to-mid kill pressure into plates, towers, and dives so the game ends before his scaling matters. If it goes long, stop trying to solo-kill him and use Ragnarok to dive past him onto his carries instead.
edits.after: Sion is the rare tank who reclaims this lane late, not early — once he has two items Soul Furnace, raw HP and Glory in Death turn him into a sponge your flat E true damage can't burn through fast enough. Killing him is not the end either: the revive brings him back with rapid attacks that heal him and scale off your max health. Don't let it get there: convert your early-to-mid kill pressure into plates, towers and dives before his scaling matters, and if it goes long use Ragnarok to dive past him onto his carries.

notes: Every Ragnarok claim here is now narrowed to the STUN on a charged Decimating Smash. Whether Olaf's disable immunity also prevents the knockup half (a displacement) is not answerable from Riot's text, so it is left unstated rather than guessed. dosFull[1].t still reads 'R to cleanse his charged Q' at 26 characters — it was left alone because rewriting a heading is not where the correction belongs, but it overstates what R does and would read better as 'R through his charged Q'.
